key_insight: ArcFlow shows that distilling diffusion teachers into a 2-step text-to-image generator is possible by learning a high-precision non-linear flow that follows the teacher's changing trajectory and tangent directions instead of using crude linear shortcuts.
problem_solved: Reduces the high inference cost of diffusion models by addressing the mismatch caused by linear shortcut distillation methods, enabling very few (2) denoising steps while preserving generation quality.
method: Non-Linear Flow Distillation: learn a smooth, high-precision non-linear mapping (flow) that tracks the teacher diffusion trajectory and its evolving tangent/velocity vectors rather than approximating with linear shortcuts.
2-Step Student Design: parametrize a compact 2-step generator that uses the distilled flow to perform two high-fidelity denoising steps conditioned on text, effectively bridging large timestep gaps.

Teacher–Student Coupling & Losses: train with objectives that align trajectories, velocities (tangent directions), and perceptual/image quality (e.g., reconstruction and feature-level losses) to preserve fidelity in very low-step regimes.
impact: Enables practical, low-latency text-to-image generation with diffusion-quality outputs using only two steps, making deployment and interactive applications (web, mobile, real-time) much more feasible for ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Trajectory diagram: teacher diffusion path (curved) vs. linear shortcut vs. learned non-linear flow (closer match) with tangent vectors shown.
Before/After image panel: side-by-side outputs from full-step diffusion, linear-distilled 2-step, and ArcFlow 2-step to show quality improvements.
Performance chart: quality metric (e.g., FID/CLIP) vs. number of steps highlighting ArcFlow at 2 steps near teacher performance.
Architecture sketch: high-level blocks showing teacher model, flow distillation module, and compact 2-step student inference pipeline.
paper_title: ArcFlow: Unleashing 2-Step Text-to-Image Generation via High-Precision Non-Linear Flow Distillation
paper_authors: Zihan Yang, Shuyuan Tu, Licheng Zhang, Qi Dai, Yu-Gang Jiang
